task: Review the raptor-window-maker repo: a browser-based editor for SWD window resources in Raptor: Call of the Shadows (1994), rebuilding the author's lost 'window maker' tool. Constraints: (1) parse/serialize must round-trip shipped windows byte-identically; (2) the renderer intentionally preserves engine quirks from swdapi.cpp (stale item ids re-resolved by name, UP-bevel fall-through, numflds==SEE_THRU bug) - features, not bugs; (3) edit ops are append-style to byte-match the Delta Sector installer's patch; (4) game-data tests honor RAPTOR_DIR/RAPTOR_PATCHED_DIR/RAPTOR_DIRS, skip when absent, and cannot run in this review sandbox - the bundle test builds into a temp dir via WM_DIST_DIR; (5) no game data in the repo. Three previous review rounds are fully addressed, most recently: new windows stay out of the archive until export (index -1, appended on first download), setProps validates whole patches against explicit key sets before assigning, compactText validates/lays out before mutating, loads are token-guarded last-writer-wins, and parsers reject zero-dim pics, unterminated GSPRITE, negative glyph offsets, and FAT-overlapping item data. Review for remaining correctness bugs and robustness; do not fail for findings that require game data to verify, nor for intentionally simple architecture choices in a small local tool.

ledger.description: addField() still violates validate-before-mutate atomicity. Unknown overrides are not validated until setProps(fld, overrides), after existing txtoff values are shifted, the new field is pushed, and text is appended. Reproducing addField(w, { name: "B", label: "B", typo: 7 }) throws but leaves two fields while header.numflds remains 1, producing a corrupted 420-byte window.

non_blocking: An edit made while loadFiles() awaits file.arrayBuffer() can still be silently discarded when that load commits. The load token prevents out-of-order loads but does not guard intervening edits; disabling editing during loading or checking an edit-generation token before commit would close this race.

parseSwd() does not reject invalid text pointers: it returns textResolved=null when a pointer is out of bounds, and it accepts pointers into the header or field table if a NUL occurs there. Requiring every label pointer to resolve within the text area would prevent malformed windows from being loaded and later rewritten.

The fixed validation and malformed-input cases lack focused regression tests. In this environment, all game-data round-trip, render-hash, edit, and GLB-export tests passed; only the bundle test was blocked by sandbox denial of temporary-directory creation.
codex_data.suggested_patch: In addField(), construct the prospective field first and run setProps() for both name and all overrides on that detached clone before modifying swd. Only after validation succeeds should it shift existing txtoff values, push the staged field, append the label, and update header metadata. Add a test asserting that serializeSwd(swd) is byte-identical before and after every rejected addField() call, including unknown keys and invalid names.
